A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AgenticIR work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original restoration experiments, degradation-recognition results, scheduling analyses, and component ablations in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds experiments with an alternative LLM and a stricter reflection threshold in Appendices C–D.

M1.justification: The default five-stage pipeline remains unchanged. Appendix D adds the experimental AgenticIR* variant, which accepts only very-low degradation severity, removing the original fallback accepting low severity. This is a limited inference adaptation.

E1.justification: Both versions use DIV2K/Flickr2K for fine-tuning and the same 16 MiO100 degradation combinations and real-world examples. Figure 15 adds examples within existing coverage. Correcting the underwater-image citation does not establish a dataset change.

E2.justification: New Tables 12–13 compare the default system with Llama-based AgenticIR and AgenticIR*, adding internal comparison variants. The external comparisons retain AirNet, PromptIR, MiOIR, DA-CLIP, InstructIR, AutoDIR, random invocation, and the existing individual-model comparisons.

E3.justification: The added experiments replace GPT-4 with Llama 3.1 405B for scheduling, tighten the reflection threshold, and evaluate runtime and tool-invocation counts. Existing data splits, fine-tuning settings, and six restoration-quality metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices C–D add two focused analyses: dependence on the scheduling LLM and the quality–cost consequences of stricter reflection. The existing experience, reflection, rollback, and scheduling-consistency analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain 60 scheduling trials per operation set and the entropy/variation-ratio analyses. The added restoration experiments introduce no reported seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing results remain unchanged. Tables 12–14 add Llama, threshold, and cost results: Llama PSNR is 21.06/20.79/18.80 across groups A/B/C versus 21.04/20.55/18.82 for default AgenticIR. Stricter reflection produces mixed quality changes and takes 137/117/174 seconds versus 48/54/78. Figure 10 adds PSNR annotations; Figure 15 adds qualitative outputs.

T1.justification: The scheduling-sensitivity definition in Appendix B.3 is unchanged, and no new theorem, proof, or derivation appears. The exploration–exploitation discussion is conceptual; changing the pseudocode wording from 'while true' to 'repeat' does not alter its mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: human-inspired restoration stages, VLM quality assessment, LLM scheduling, and self-exploration-derived experience. New appendix evidence supports these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Appendix C attributes similar LLM performance to experience simplifying scheduling. Appendix D newly discusses exploitation bias, premature stopping, and the quality–efficiency tradeoff. The original limitation concerning single-degradation tools is retained, moving from Appendix C to E.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 newly identifies gpt-4-1106-preview. The additions specify Llama 3.1 405B, the stricter acceptance rule, and runtime/tool-use measurements. The underwater-image source is corrected; existing training details, prompts, toolbox, and code-access information remain available.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Berger-Tal et al. on exploration–exploitation, the Llama technical report, and Islam et al. for underwater imagery. The positioning relative to existing restoration and agent research remains stable; other reference edits mainly update metadata.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording, tense, capitalization, and workflow-explanation edits, updates publication and affiliation text, and adds appendix subsections. The main narrative structure is retained, and the limitations paragraph is relocated without substantive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 12–14 and Figure 15, annotates Figure 10 with PSNR values, and makes limited caption and spacing changes. Existing figures and tables are retained within substantially the same visual organization.

improvement.justification: The alternative-LLM test and measured reflection tradeoff provide useful evidence about portability and computational cost that v1 lacked. Model-version disclosure and corrected data attribution also improve reproducibility. The gains are limited: threshold effects are mixed, and the explanation attributing LLM differences to randomness is not supported by new uncertainty estimates.
